Yadu
------------------------------------------
The famous ancestor of the यदु-vaṁśa or the Yādava clan, यदु was the eldest son of the king ययाति and his queen Devayānī, daughter of शुक्राचार्य, the teacher of the असुरस् (demons). Since he refused to take the old-age of his ड़थेर् in exchange for his youth, he lost his right to succeed his ड़थेर्. कृष्ण belonged to his clan.

Yādavaprakāśa
(Eleventh century A. D.)
------------------------------------------
Yādavaprakāśa was a reputed teacher of Advaita Vedānta under whom Rāmānuja (A.

-1137) studied for some time. Since Rāmānuja’s genius did not accept the dry interpretation of the उपनिषद्स् sans भक्ति or devotion to God, differences arose between them. According to one view, यादवप्रकाश had planned to get Rāmānuja drowned in the गङ्गा river during a पिल्ग्रिमगे, but he managed to escape. Later on, it is said, यादवप्रकाश became a disciple of Rāmānuja under the baptismal name Govindadāsa. The book Yatidharmasamuccaya is said to be his composition.
See also RĀMĀNUJĀCĀRYA.
